title: AI Now’s Co-Executive Director Amba Kak Testifies Before Monopoly Busters Caucus
content:
On Thursday, September 17th, 2026, AI Now Co-Executive Director Amba Kak testified before the Monopoly Busters Caucus at the shadow hearing “AI Crossroads: Stopping Big Tech’s Race to Monopolize AI through Surveillance on Big Tech.” The hearing came amidst a frenzy of alarmist claims about the existential threat of AI and calls from within the tech industry itself for regulation. In her testimony, Ms. Kak warned against the AI industry’s vision to further centralize power within a small group of private actors, and called on our representatives to act to protect the public from the consequences of a surveillance economy. She outlined three recommendations:

  • Go after root causes, not symptoms.
  • Don’t let companies co-opt the solution space.
  • End AI exceptionalism and enforce the laws on the books.

title: Will AI really kill everyone? How, exactly?
content:
“Scientific claims require falsifiability precisely to avoid the nature of religious arguments,” said Heidy Khlaaf, chief AI scientist at the AI Now Institute and a former OpenAI safety engineer. “You need to be able to prove or disprove them.”

Then there are nuclear weapons, which have existed for more than 80 years and are generally understood to be capable of killing off all human life. Could AI commandeer them?

Khlaaf points out that nuclear facilities are “air-gapped” from the publicly accessible internet, which limits the ways AI agents could get at the controls. “These systems are built to a completely different, rigorous and regulated engineering standard that often requires physical hardening,” she said. Stuxnet, the computer worm that damaged Iran’s nuclear facilities, had to be introduced to the system through a physical USB drive, she noted.

title: Independent Contractor Role: AI Now seeks a Local Policy Researcher/Land Use Expert
content:
AI Now is looking for a consultant to support a research project focused on data center expansion. The Researcher will work with AI Now and Local Progress to (1) create three
state-specific guides to local data center policy and (2) update our research template for other
states.

This project aims to address this gap of state-specific recommendations, building on AI Now’s North Star Data Center Toolkit, which maps the strongest possible local, state, and federal policy interventions to stop and slow the data center buildout. We developed this resource in response to and in collaboration with numerous fights on the ground, as existing guides were either issue-specific or took a less-than-transformative approach. The toolkit has been successfully used across the US, primarily to set policy at the local and state-level, but we have not yet been able to offer state-by-state specifics.

title: Could AI really wipe out humanity – six experts spell out the risks
content:
There have been some shocking claims in recent days about AI safety: we face a 10% chance of doom; AIs are worse than nukes; a “botnet” threatens the entire internet; it’s all a big tech psyop.

But Heidy Khlaaf, chief scientist at the AI Now Institute research body, is among experts sceptical about giving percentage chances to existential scenarios.

“These claims are neither falsifiable nor verifiable, making then unscientific by their very nature,” she said. The shortage of concrete examples of what a “superintelligent” AI might do to cause “doom” only adds to the cloudiness. A source familiar with Anthropic’s thinking acknowledges that “the exact chances of any one outcome are probably unknowable”.

“If you cannot provide such evidence, it also implies whatever numbers you produced for ‘extinction’ have no scientific basis,” Khlaaf added. Critics say such numbers borrow the authority of science without doing the work.

title: Why this AI doomsday warning from former Anthropic researcher broke through
content:
“It’s been at least over a year of steadily increasing data center pushback that has made being pro-AI regulation the new common sense, and it certainly has made being pro-AI industry a very toxic brand,” said Amba Kak, co-executive director of the AI Now Institute and a former senior adviser on AI for the US Federal Trade Commission.

“It allowed for companies like Anthropic and others to position themselves immediately as the primary experts in how to deal with these fears. How to solve problems that, by every account, they have created or are best positioned to prevent,” Kak said.

title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
content:
Aya Ibrahim, who leads national security work for the AI Now Institute, an independent research organization, said that any limitations of AI predictions may get little scrutiny from elected officials. Policymakers have a track record of being deferential when dealing with the tech sector, she said.

“When it comes to tech issues, there’s just this culture of learned helplessness from the same policymakers that sit on energy and commerce [committees] and oversee the FDA and prescription drugs,” topics where they don’t question their right to govern, said Ibrahim, a former Biden White House official. “Suddenly, if you can’t code the model yourself, then you’re not in a position to weigh in.”

title: What’s really motivating these AI apocalypse stories?
content:
AI Now’s co-executive director Sarah Myers West joins Al Jazeera’s The Listening Post to talk about regulating the tech industry, and the familiar race to the bottom we see playing out in front of us.

“Time and again, whenever we’ve seen any movement toward meaningful regulation of the tech industry, we see a revival of this [race] narrative,” says Myers West. “What this narrative mistakes though is that regulation of the sector actually would be a tremendous boon to competition. Nobody is helped if we have an unregulated sector that’s engaged in the race to the bottom. That’s what we’re seeing right here and now.”
